classification.difficultyReason: Interpret an upper-tail percentage using the empirical rule, then work backwards by one standard deviation to find the mean.

content.prompt: A normal distribution has a standard deviation of 3. If 16% of the scores are at least 29, find the mean.

answer.worked:
By the empirical rule, 16% of scores lie above one standard deviation above the mean. Thus 29 has $z=1$.

$$\begin{aligned}29&=\mu+3\\\mu&=29-3\\\mu&=26\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Authored solution sketch following the page 28 instruction to sketch the normal curve with corresponding raw scores. The upper tail beyond 29 is shaded.
spec.mathematics: Mean 26, standard deviation 3; 29 is one standard deviation above the mean, with an empirical-rule upper-tail area of 16%.
